s: 新人の私が会議室のドアを（　　）、中から一斉に拍手が起こり、思わずその場に立ち止まった。
en: The instant I, the new hire, opened the meeting room door, applause broke out inside, and I stopped dead.
why: たとたん marks your own quick action followed by a surprise, and 思わず shows the surprise.
かと思うと is only for someone else you are watching, never for 私.
次第 must be followed by a plan or request, not by a past surprise.
最中 needs an activity that lasts a while; opening a door is over in a moment.
tell: Your own momentary action plus a surprise → たとたん. かと思うと never has 私 as subject.

s: カードを紛失した（　　）は、ただちに下記の番号までご連絡ください。
en: If you lose your card, please call the number below immediately.
why: 際 is the formal 'when' for notices, and it takes た形 (紛失した際は).
にあたって needs a planned one-off milestone and a noun or dictionary form; losing a card is neither.
に先立って means 'before, as preparation' and takes a noun, not た形.
最中 needs ている形 or a noun and an activity in progress.
tell: Notice + た形 + は + request → 際は. にあたって is for planned milestones only.

s: 同僚の愚痴に毎日付き合っている（　　）、気づけば自分も会社への不満ばかり口にするようになっていた。
en: From keeping a colleague company through his complaints every day, I found I had started grumbling about the company all the time myself.
why: うちに (B): while doing something for a while, a change crept in by itself; 気づけば〜ていた confirms it.
最中に marks one activity in progress that gets interrupted, not a slow change built up over days.
つつ attaches to the ます stem (付き合いつつ), never to ている.
次第 attaches to the ます stem and is followed by a plan, never a past change.
tell: ている + うちに + a change you only noticed later (気づけば〜ていた). 最中 wants an interruption.

s: 長く低迷していた地方の景気も、ここ一、二年は徐々にではあるが、ようやく（　　）。
en: The regional economy, sluggish for years, has finally been picking up over the last year or two, if only gradually.
c: 持ち直そうとしている
why: つつある shows a change already under way, and 徐々に over ここ一、二年 describes exactly that.
ようとしている is the edge just before a change starts, but 徐々に shows the recovery is already moving.
一方だ is a relentless one-way trend, which clashes with ようやく (finally).
ばかりだ leans toward bad trends, and it also clashes with ようやく.
tell: A change already moving over a period (徐々に・少しずつ) → つつある. ようとしている is only the edge before it.

s: 部長は「残業を減らせ」と（　　）、自分は毎晩遅くまで会社に残っている。
en: The department head tells us to cut overtime, yet he himself stays at the office late every night.
why: A speech verb + つつ means 'although': he says one thing and does the opposite.
つつある shows a change in progress, and 言う is not a change verb.
につれて links two gradual changes, and there is no gradual change here.
たとたん is one instant then a surprise, but 残っている is an ongoing habit.
tell: Speech or mind verb + つつ = although (said X, did the opposite). Change verb + つつある = in progress.

s: このアプリは、本人確認の手続きを（　　）仕組みになっている。
en: This app is set up so that you cannot send money until you have completed identity verification.
c: 済ませてからでないと送金できない
済ませてからでないと送金できる
済ませた上で送金できない
済ませて以来送金できない
why: てからでないと must be followed by a negative: unless you do X first, you can't.
てからでないと never takes a positive result after it.
上で leads into a deliberate next step, not into 'can't'.
て以来 describes a state since a past point, which makes no sense for a rule.
tell: てからでないと locks in a negative ending: 〜てからでないと〜できない.

s: 自分が部下を（　　）、上司がどれほど気を配ってくれていたかに気づいた。
en: Only after I had staff of my own did I notice how much care my boss had taken over me.
why: てはじめて: only after the experience did a realisation come, here 気づいた.
上で leads into a deliberate second step, and noticing is not a deliberate act.
てからでないと must end in a negative.
て以来 needs a state that continues to now, not a one-off realisation.
tell: Experience first, then a realisation that wasn't possible before (気づく・わかる) → てはじめて.

s: 三年前に今の部署へ（　　）、定時に帰れた日は一日もない。
en: Since I moved to my current department three years ago, I haven't left on time a single day.
c: 異動してからでないと
why: て以来: from a past point up to now, the same state has held; 一日もない confirms it.
てはじめて is for a new realisation, not a state that has run for three years.
上で leads into a deliberate next step, not a lasting state.
てからでないと sets a condition still to be met, but 三年前に is a past fact.
tell: Past point + a state that runs to now (一度も／一日も〜ない) → て以来.

s: お申し込み内容をご確認いただいた（　　）、ページ下部の送信ボタンを押してください。
en: After checking your application details, please press the submit button at the bottom of the page.
why: た形 + 上で: do step one properly, then step two; a request after is fine.
上に stacks two things of the same kind and cannot lead into a request.
とたんに must be followed by a surprise, never a request.
かと思うと is for watching someone else and refuses requests.
tell: Check first, then act, with a request after → た上で. 上に only stacks evaluations.

s: この会計ソフトは操作が複雑な（　　）、動作も遅いので、社内での評判はよくない。
en: This accounting software is complicated to use and slow on top of that, so it has a poor reputation in the office.
why: 上に stacks two points of the same kind: complicated, and slow too.
上で means 'after doing' and needs a verb in た形, not ナ形な.
うちに means 'while it is still ~' and makes no sense with a fixed property.
ものの means 'although', but both points are negative and も adds rather than contrasts.
tell: Bad + bad (or good + good) with も after → 上に. 上で is 'after doing'.

s: 審査の結果が（　　）、担当者よりメールでお知らせいたします。
en: As soon as the review results are out, the person in charge will let you know by email.
why: ます stem + 次第 = as soon as, followed by the speaker's plan (お知らせいたします).
たとたん cannot be followed by the speaker's intention.
かと思うと describes what you watched happen and cannot lead into a promise.
次第では means 'depending on' and attaches to a noun, not a verb.
tell: Verb stem + 次第 = as soon as → a promise or request. Noun + 次第 = depends on.

s: 契約を更新してもらえるかどうかは、今期の（　　）次第だ。
en: Whether they renew our contract depends on this term's sales.
why: Noun + 次第だ = depends on; かどうかは sets up exactly that.
Verb stem + 次第 (伸び次第) means 'as soon as' and cannot end the sentence with だ.
Dictionary form + 次第だ is the stiff 'that is why' (お願いする次第です), not 'depends on'.
た形 + 次第だ explains how something came about (ご連絡した次第です), not 'depends on'.
tell: 〜かどうかは + noun + 次第だ = it depends on. Stem + 次第 is 'as soon as'.

s: 担当者に確認した（　　）、今回の値上げは来年度以降の契約にのみ適用されるそうです。
en: As far as I could confirm with the person in charge, this price rise applies only to contracts from next year on.
why: Info verb (確認した) + 限りでは = as far as my information goes, then a hedged report.
に限って complains that bad luck struck on exactly that occasion; it is not a hedged report.
にかけては praises a skill and follows a noun.
に限り follows a noun on notices to mark the only case that qualifies.
tell: Info verb (調べた・確認した・聞いた) + 限りでは → a hedged report.

s: よりによって大事な面接がある日（　　）、朝から電車が止まったりパソコンが固まったりする。
en: Of all days, it's always the day of an important interview that the trains stop and my computer freezes.
why: に限って: on exactly the day you need things to go well, bad luck strikes; よりによって says the same.
に限り is for notices: only this case qualifies for something.
に限らず means 'not only on that day', which clashes with よりによって.
限りでは needs an info verb like 調べた before it.
tell: よりによって + the day you need luck + bad things happen → に限って.

s: 本人が自分から（　　）、周りが何を言っても状況は変わらないだろう。
en: Unless he himself tries to change, nothing will change, whatever the people around him say.
c: 変わろうとしない限り
変わろうとしない限りでは
変わろうとしないに限って
変わろうとしないに限り
why: ない限り = unless; the negative judgement 変わらないだろう follows.
限りでは needs an info verb (見た・聞いた) and gives a hedged report.
に限って follows a noun and complains about bad luck.
に限り is notice language for the one case that qualifies.
tell: 〜ない限り = unless → a negative outcome. 限りでは only follows info verbs.

s: 社長への要望は、直接ではなく各部の部長（　　）伝えることになっている。
en: Requests to the president are meant to go through each department head, not directly.
why: を通して = via a go-between person; 直接ではなく sets that up.
にわたって covers a large span of time or space, not a person.
をもとに means making something new from source material.
のもとで means working under a person's guidance, not passing a message through them.
tell: Not directly, but through a person → を通して. にわたって is for big spans.

s: A「この店、平日も混んでるの？」　B「うん、週末（　　）、いつ来てもこんな感じだよ。」
en: A: Is this place busy on weekdays too? B: Yeah, not just weekends. It's like this whenever you come.
why: に限らず = not just X but a wider range; いつ来ても says it is busy at any time.
に限って means 'only on that occasion, unusually', which contradicts いつ来ても.
に限り marks the only case that qualifies, which also contradicts いつ来ても.
上に stacks two evaluations and needs の after a noun (週末の上に).
tell: The range is wider than X (いつ来ても・誰でも) → に限らず. に限って／に限り narrow it to X.

s: 田中さんは大事な会議に遅れて来た（　　）、配るはずの資料まで家に忘れてきた。
en: Not only did Tanaka turn up late to an important meeting, he even left the handouts at home.
why: ばかりか takes a full clause and escalates to something worse, marked by まで.
に限らず attaches only to a noun, not to a clause like 遅れて来た.
はもとより attaches to a noun, not to a clause.
上で means 'after doing (as preparation)', not 'on top of that'.
tell: Clause + something even worse with まで → ばかりか. に限らず／はもとより need a noun.

s: この祭りは、地元で（　　）、県外から訪れる観光客の間でも広く知られている。
en: This festival is well known locally, of course, and widely known among visitors from other prefectures too.
why: はもとより can follow a particle (地元で) and treats that first item as obvious.
に限らず attaches straight to a noun and cannot follow で.
上に stacks two clauses and cannot follow で.
をはじめ follows a bare noun and needs a group word after it.
tell: Particle + はもとより (地元ではもとより): X goes without saying, Y too.

s: 父の残した土地（　　）、兄弟が十年近くも争ってきた。
en: The brothers have been fighting over the land their father left for nearly ten years.
why: をめぐって: several parties in a dispute over something; 兄弟が争う confirms it.
にかけては is praise for a skill nobody beats.
に対して aims an action at a target, but you don't fight 'at' the land.
に応じて adjusts something to a variable, which makes no sense here.
tell: Several people + 争う・対立・議論 → をめぐって.

s: 都市部の人口が増え続けている（　　）、山間部では空き家が目立つようになった。
en: Whereas the urban population keeps growing, empty houses have become a common sight in the mountain areas.
why: Clause + の + に対して = whereas: city and mountains are a stated contrast.
Without の, に対して follows a noun and means 'toward'.
につれて follows the dictionary form directly and links two gradual changes in the same place.
をめぐって is for a dispute among several parties.
tell: A is X, whereas B is Y (a stated contrast) → clause + のに対して.

s: お客様からいただいたご意見（　　）、担当部署が責任を持って一つ一つお答えいたします。
en: The department in charge will take responsibility for answering each comment we receive from customers.
why: Noun + に対して = toward a target: answering the comments.
のに対して sets up a contrast between two clauses, and there is none here.
をめぐっては is for disputes among several parties.
にかけては praises a skill nobody can beat.
tell: Noun + に対して + respond (答える・対応する) = toward. の + に対して = whereas.

s: 地元の人たちの期待（　　）、彼女は引退を撤回して、もう一年現役を続けることにした。
en: Answering the hopes of local people, she took back her retirement and decided to compete for one more year.
why: にこたえて goes with 期待・要望 and means acting to meet them.
に応じて adjusts to something that varies, like a budget or age; an expectation is not a variable.
をもとに means making something new out of source material.
にわたって covers a large span of time or space.
tell: 期待・要望・声援 + にこたえて. A variable (予算・年齢) + に応じて.

s: 宿泊料金は季節や曜日（　　）細かく変わるので、予約の前に必ず確認してほしい。
en: Room rates change in small steps with the season and the day of the week, so please check before booking.
why: に応じて: something is adjusted to a variable, here the season and day.
にこたえて only goes with expectations or requests (期待・要望).
にわたって covers a large span and does not mean 'according to'.
をめぐって is for disputes among several parties.
tell: Changes to match a variable (季節・予算・年齢) → に応じて.

s: この漫画は、作者が若いころに離島で過ごした体験（　　）描かれている。
en: This manga draws on the author's experience of living on a remote island when young.
why: をもとに: a new work is made from source material, here an experience; 描かれている is the creation verb.
に応じて adjusts something to a variable (予算・年齢), and a past experience is not a variable.
向けに means 'made for' a target group, and 体験 is not a group of people.
のもとで means 'under' a person's guidance or a condition.
tell: Source material + creation verb (作る・描く・書く) → をもとに.

s: 感覚に頼るのではなく、データ（　　）判断が求められている。
en: What is needed is judgement grounded in data, not reliance on gut feeling.
why: に基づいた + noun: judging by a criterion such as data or law.
のもとでの needs a person or a condition (管理・了解), and data is neither.
向けの means 'made for' a target group of people.
にこたえる only goes with expectations or requests.
cue: 感覚に頼るのではなく
tell: Criterion (データ・法律・根拠) + に基づいた + 判断.

s: このスマートフォンは、操作に慣れていない高齢者（　　）、文字やボタンが大きく設計されている。
en: This smartphone is designed for older people who aren't used to the controls, with large text and buttons.
why: 向けに: deliberately made for a target group, with a design verb after.
をもとに needs source material, and people are not material.
に沿って follows a plan or policy, not a group of users.
に基づいて needs a criterion like data or law, not a group of people.
tell: Target group of people + design verb (作る・設計する) → 向けに.

s: 高速道路の開通（　　）、沿線の町には大型の商業施設が次々に建てられた。
en: With the opening of the expressway, large shopping centres went up one after another in the towns along it.
why: に伴って links a change seen as a whole, here a one-off opening, to the changes that followed.
につれて needs a gradual change before it, but an opening happens once.
うちに needs something that lasts a while, not a one-off 開通.
に応じて adjusts something to a variable, and the opening is not a variable.
tell: A change seen as a whole (開通・増加) → に伴って. につれて needs a gradual change.

s: うちの上司は、資料の字が小さい（　　）色が地味だのと、中身以外のことばかり細かく指摘してくる。
en: My boss keeps nitpicking at everything except the content: the font is too small, the colours are dull, and so on.
why: だの〜だの is a fed-up list of complaints, and the pair must match (地味だのと).
やら must pair with やら, and it shows overwhelm, not complaint.
というか offers two labels for one impression, not a list of complaints.
といった wraps up examples and must be followed by a noun.
tell: A fed-up list of complaints → 〜だの〜だの. Paired forms must match.

s: 出席するにしても欠席する（　　）、今週中に幹事に返事をしてください。
en: Whether you attend or not, please reply to the organiser this week.
why: にしても〜にしても pairs two options and gives the same advice either way.
としたら is a single supposition, and a pair opened with にしても must close with にしても.
とすると cannot be followed by a request like 返事をしてください.
ものなら needs a potential verb and a wish.
tell: Two options, same advice either way → 〜にしても〜にしても.

s: 大型の台風が接近している（　　）、その選手は予定どおり海に出ると言い張った。
en: Even though a big typhoon was approaching, the athlete insisted on going out to sea as planned.
why: にもかかわらず (with も) = even though: a real fact had no effect, to our surprise.
にかかわらず (no も) = regardless of a range or pair, not one fact.
を問わず needs a width word or an opposing pair (年齢・男女).
ばかりに needs a bad result caused by the first clause, not a stubborn choice.
tell: One real fact + a surprising action anyway → にもかかわらず. No も = regardless of a range.

s: 学生（　　）、社会人が連絡もなく会議を休むのは許されることではない。
en: It might be one thing for a student, but for a working adult to miss a meeting without notice is unacceptable.
why: ならともかく = X would be one thing, but; it parks X to stress what follows.
さておき drops a topic already under discussion and never follows なら.
でさえ means 'even X', which makes students the extreme case and breaks the logic.
にとって gives someone's viewpoint and leaves 社会人が with no link.
cue: 許されることではない
tell: X would be one thing, but Y is not OK → 〜ならともかく. さておき never takes なら.

s: 大きな地震のあとは、何は（　　）、まず家族の無事を確かめることが大切だ。
en: After a big earthquake, before anything else, the important thing is to check that your family is safe.
why: 何はさておき is the set phrase for 'before anything else': drop everything and do the main thing first.
かまわず needs も (人目もかまわず) and means ignoring what one should mind.
もとより needs a real first item and a following 〜も (平日はもとより週末も).
問わず needs を and a width word or pair (年齢を問わず).
tell: Before anything else → 何はさておき (set phrase). Xはさておき drops X to get to the main point.

s: 経験年数の長い社員が、必ずしも新しいシステムの扱いに慣れている（　　）。
en: Employees with long experience are not necessarily used to handling the new system.
why: 必ずしも calls for a partial denial: わけではない.
わけがない is a total denial and clashes with 必ずしも.
ものか is an angry spoken denial and doesn't follow 必ずしも.
ことはない means 'no need to', which doesn't fit a statement about people.
tell: 必ずしも → partial denial: 〜わけではない／〜とは限らない.

s: 広告費をかければ、それだけ商品が売れる（　　）。広告が売り上げにつながることもあるが、まったくつながらないことも多い。
en: Spending more on advertising doesn't automatically mean you sell more. Ads sometimes lead to sales, but often they lead to none at all.
why: 〜ば〜というものではない denies a rule of thumb: the condition does not guarantee the result, as the next sentence spells out.
わけがない says it is impossible, but the next sentence says ads sometimes do lead to sales.
わけだ draws the conclusion that sales follow, which the next sentence contradicts.
どころではない means there is no time or room for something.
cue: つながることもあるが
tell: 〜ば + result that only sometimes follows → 〜というものではない (not automatically).

s: A「駅前の大きな本屋、今月で閉店するんだって。」　B「え、あんなにお客さんが入っている店が閉店する（　　）。誰かの勘違いじゃない？」
en: A: I heard the big bookshop by the station is closing this month. B: What? There's no way a shop with that many customers would close. Hasn't someone got it wrong?
why: わけがない = there's no way; B is sure the report is wrong, so 誰かの勘違い follows.
わけではない is only a partial denial (not entirely), so it gives no grounds for calling the report a mistake.
どころではない means having no time or room for something.
というものではない denies a general rule of thumb, not a specific report.
cue: あんなにお客さんが入っている
誰かの勘違いじゃない
tell: Certain it can't be true → 〜わけがない. わけではない is only 'not entirely'.

s: A「来月、うちの部署から五人も異動するんだって。」　B「それで最近、部長があんなに急いで採用を進めている（　　）。」
en: A: I heard five people are being transferred out of our department next month. B: So that's why the manager has been rushing to hire people lately.
why: わけだ = it follows, no wonder; それで links the news to what B has seen.
わけがない denies something B can see is happening.
わけではない is a partial denial, and nothing is being denied.
わけにはいかない is the speaker's own social bind, but B is explaining the manager's behaviour.
tell: それで + a fact that now makes sense → 〜わけだ (no wonder).

s: お世話になった恩師の退職祝いの会なのだから、いくら忙しくても（　　）。
en: It's the retirement party for a teacher who did so much for me, so however busy I am, I have to show up.
c: 顔を出さないわけにはいかない
顔を出すわけにはいかない
顔を出さないわけではない
why: ないわけにはいかない = must, out of social obligation; owing the teacher creates that duty.
わけにはいかない without ない means 'can't go', the opposite of where いくら忙しくても leads.
ないわけではない is a weak partial denial and doesn't express duty.
わけがない would mean 'no way I'd go', which contradicts the reason given.
tell: Social duty + いくら〜ても → 〜ないわけにはいかない (must).

s: A「その飲み会、無理して行かなくてもいいんじゃない？」　B「でも、自分の送別会だから、主役が（　　）よ。」
en: A: You don't have to force yourself to go to that party, do you? B: But it's my own farewell party. The guest of honour can't very well skip it.
c: 欠席するわけにはいかない
欠席しないわけにはいかない
欠席するどころではない
why: わけにはいかない: social reasons stop me, here because I'm the guest of honour.
ないわけにはいかない means 'I must skip it', the opposite of B's point.
わけだ draws a conclusion, but B is pushing back on A's suggestion.
どころではない means having no time or room for something.
tell: Socially I can't (it's my duty as the 主役) → 〜わけにはいかない.

s: 年度末で毎日終電近くまで働いているので、週末に旅行の計画を立てる（　　）。
en: It's the end of the financial year and I'm working until nearly the last train every day, so planning a weekend trip is out of the question.
why: どころではない: no time or energy to spare for something, here because of overwork.
どころか needs a second clause that goes further; it can't end the sentence.
にすぎない means 'merely', which doesn't fit the reason given.
わけだ draws a conclusion, but planning a trip doesn't follow from overwork.
cue: 終電近くまで働いているので
tell: No time, money or calm for X → X + どころではない. どころか needs a second clause.

s: 雨の予報が出ていたので客足が落ちると心配していたが、落ちる（　　）、開店以来の売り上げを記録した。
en: With rain forecast, I'd worried customers would stay away, but far from it, we recorded our best sales since opening.
why: どころか: far from X, the opposite happened, here record sales.
どころではなく means there's no room for something, not 'the opposite happened'.
ばかりに needs a single cause leading to a bad result.
わけがなく is certainty that X can't happen, but the speaker was worried it would.
tell: Expected X, got the opposite → X + どころか.

s: 細かいことには無頓着な姉だが、コーヒー豆（　　）、産地から焙煎の具合まで一切妥協しない。
en: My sister doesn't fuss over details, but when it comes to coffee beans, she won't compromise on anything, from the origin to the roast.
why: (のこと)となると: when this subject comes up, the person acts unlike their usual self.
といえば says what springs to mind from X, not how someone behaves when X comes up.
とは introduces a definition.
にとって gives someone's viewpoint plus an evaluation, and it cannot take an action like 妥協しない.
tell: Normally X, but on this one subject they act differently → 〜(のこと)となると.

s: A「新しいオフィス、駅から遠くて不便じゃない？」　B「不便（　　）不便だけど、そのぶん家賃がかなり安いんだよ。」
en: A: Isn't the new office inconvenient, so far from the station? B: Inconvenient, sure, but the rent is much cheaper because of it.
why: X といえば X だけど: grant the point, then give the real one.
ことは needs な after a ナ形 adjective: 不便なことは不便だ.
とは introduces a definition and doesn't repeat the word.
となると shows a change when a topic comes up, not a concession.
tell: Same word twice + けど: concede, then the real point. ナ形 + ことは needs な.

s: あの店のラーメンのまずさ（　　）、一口食べただけで箸を置いてしまったほどだ。
en: That shop's ramen was so bad that I put my chopsticks down after one bite.
why: Quality noun (まずさ) + といったら: the degree was beyond normal, shown by ほどだ.
とは introduces a definition.
となると shows a person changing when a topic comes up.
というと says what comes to mind or checks a meaning, not an extreme degree.
tell: Quality noun (〜さ) + といったら + an extreme result → beyond words.

s: A「週末はジムに通ってるんだって？」　B「通ってる（　　）、月に二回サウナに入りに行くくらいだよ。」
en: A: I hear you go to the gym at weekends? B: I say go, but it's just to use the sauna twice a month.
why: といっても: I say X, but the reality is smaller, here only the sauna.
からといって needs a denial like とは限らない after it.
ながらも joins a state to an unexpected result, not a correction of an image.
にもかかわらず is formal and marks surprise that a fact had no effect.
tell: I say X, but it's less than it sounds (〜くらいだ) → 〜といっても.

s: ゴルフの道具を高いものでそろえた（　　）、すぐに上達するとは限らない。
en: Just because you've bought expensive golf gear doesn't mean you'll improve quickly.
why: からといって pairs with とは限らない: just because X doesn't mean Y.
からには leads to resolve or duty (now that X, I will), not to とは限らない.
ながらも joins a state to an actual result, not a general claim.
にもかかわらず marks surprise at an actual result, not a general claim.
tell: 〜とは限らない／〜わけではない at the end → からといって at the start.

s: 新しい家計簿アプリを（　　）、入力が面倒で三日しか続かなかった。
en: I installed a new budgeting app, but entering everything was a pain and I only kept it up for three days.
c: 入れてみたからといって
why: ものの: X really happened, but the expected follow-up did not.
からといって needs a denial like とは限らない after it.
つつも needs a mind or speech verb (思う・知る), not an action like installing.
ながらも needs a state word, not a one-off action.
cue: 三日しか続かなかった
tell: Did X, but the expected next step failed → 〜たものの.

s: うちの犬は、私が少しでも出かける準備を（　　）、玄関の前に座り込んで動かなくなる。
en: If I so much as start getting ready to go out, my dog sits down in front of the door and won't budge.
why: Volitional + ものなら: if you dared do even that, trouble follows; 少しでも sets it up.
Potential + ものなら is a wish (if only I could), not a threat.
としたら is pure supposition, but this is the dog's real habit.
としても means 'even if', which reverses the logic.
tell: 少しでも + volitional + ものなら → trouble follows. Potential + ものなら is a wish.

s: このコースは、パソコンとネット環境（　　）、自宅からでも受講できます。
en: As long as you have a computer and an internet connection, you can take this course from home.
why: さえ〜ば: this one condition is enough for the result (受講できます).
ものなら after a verb is a wish and needs a potential verb, which ある is not.
Volitional + ものなら warns of disaster, but the result here is good.
としても means 'even if' and reverses the logic.
tell: Just this one condition and it works → 〜さえ〜ば.

s: A「部長に出した企画書、間違いだらけだったんだって？」　B「うん。取り戻せる（　　）、今すぐ取り戻したいよ。」
en: A: I heard the proposal you gave the manager was full of mistakes? B: Yeah. If I could get it back, I'd get it back right now.
why: Potential verb + ものなら + a wish: if only I could.
とすると cannot be followed by the speaker's wish (取り戻したい).
としても means 'even if', which turns the wish upside down.
からには means 'now that', but B cannot actually get it back.
tell: Potential verb + ものなら + 〜たい: if only I could.

s: 日本の近代化の歴史は、鉄道の（　　）語ることができない。
en: You cannot tell the story of Japan's modernisation without the development of the railways.
c: 発達してからでないと
why: を抜きにしては: leave out a highly valued X and something can't be done; 語ることができない follows.
ないことには sets a condition still to be met, but this history has already happened.
てからでないと sets a first step still to come, which doesn't fit a past history.
ない限り sets an ongoing condition, not a missing part of a story.
tell: Leave out a valued X and you can't tell or do Y → 〜を抜きにしては.

s: お待たせしてすみません。前の打ち合わせが長引いてしまった（　　）。
en: Sorry to keep you waiting. My previous meeting ran over.
why: ものですから gives a personal excuse after an apology and can end the sentence.
おかげ is for a result you are grateful for, and keeping someone waiting is not one.
ことですし gives a light reason for 'let's', and nothing is being proposed.
あまり needs too much of a feeling leading to an extreme reaction.
tell: Apology + personal excuse → 〜ものですから. おかげ is only for good results.

s: 【お知らせ】エレベーター点検（　　）、本日10時から12時までは階段をご利用ください。
en: Notice: Due to lift maintenance, please use the stairs today from 10:00 to 12:00.
why: につき gives the reason for the current situation on signs and notices.
ものだから is a spoken personal excuse and cannot be followed by a request.
おかげで is for a good result.
あまり means too much of something, not a scheduled reason.
tell: Sign or notice + reason for the current situation → noun + につき.

s: 孫の合格の知らせを聞いた祖母は、うれしさの（　　）、その場で泣き出してしまった。
en: When she heard her grandson had passed, my grandmother was so happy she burst into tears on the spot.
why: Noun + の + あまり: so much of a feeling that an unusual reaction follows.
おかげで needs a result you are grateful for, and bursting into tears (てしまった) is not one.
ものだから is a personal excuse and needs な after a noun.
につき gives a reason on notices.
tell: Too much of a feeling (緊張・うれしさ) → an unusual reaction: 〜のあまり.

s: A「今日はみんな頑張った（　　）、帰りに軽く何か食べていかない？」
en: A: Everyone worked hard today, so why don't we grab a bite on the way home?
why: ことだし gives a light reason and leads into 'let's'.
ばかりに leads to a regretted bad result and cannot be followed by an invitation.
だけに cannot be followed by an invitation.
ものの means 'although', which doesn't link a reason to a suggestion.
tell: Light reason + let's / shall we → 〜ことだし.

s: 新しいもの好きの姉（　　）、発売日の朝から店の前に並んでいるに違いない。
en: Knowing my sister and her love of new things, she must be queuing outside the shop from the morning of the release.
why: Person + のことだから: knowing them, I make a guess (に違いない).
ばかりに needs a single cause and a regretted bad result.
だけあって praises what has been shown and cannot be followed by a guess.
からには follows a clause, not a bare noun, and leads to resolve.
tell: Person + のことだから + a guess about them (だろう・に違いない).

s: 自分から「やります」と手を挙げた（　　）、どんなに大変でも最後までやり抜くつもりだ。
en: Now that I've volunteered myself, I intend to see it through to the end, however hard it is.
why: からには: now that X, I will; it leads into resolve (つもりだ).
だけに cannot be followed by the speaker's intention.
ばかりに leads to a regretted result and cannot be followed by an intention.
ものの means 'although', which doesn't lead into resolve.
tell: Now that X + resolve (〜つもりだ・〜なければ) → 〜からには.

s: 準備に半年もかけた（　　）、雨で中止が決まったときの落胆は大きかった。
en: Precisely because we had spent half a year preparing, we were deeply disappointed when it was cancelled for rain.
why: だけに: because of X, a fitting and stronger feeling follows, here disappointment.
だけあって praises a result that lives up to X, and a letdown is not praise.
わりに marks a result off the level you'd expect, but a big letdown is exactly what half a year of work leads you to expect.
からといって needs a denial like とは限らない after it.
tell: Big effort or hopes + a fittingly bigger letdown → 〜だけに.

s: 犯人の顔は見ていないので、警察に特徴を聞かれても（　　）。
en: I didn't see the culprit's face, so even if the police ask what he looked like, I have no way to answer.
c: 答えるどころではない
答えるわけにはいかない
why: ようがない: there is no method at all, because I didn't see the face.
どころではない means having no time or calm for something.
にすぎない means 'merely', which makes no sense here.
わけにはいかない is a social bind, but the problem here is missing information.
tell: No information, no way at all → ます stem + ようがない.

s: 長年信頼してきた友人に裏切られたことは、今でも（　　）。
en: Being betrayed by a friend I had trusted for years is something I still find hard to accept.
c: 受け入れるどころではない
why: がたい with a mind verb: emotionally hard to accept.
た形 + ものだ is a fond memory of a past habit, not a present feeling.
どころではない means no time or room for something.
得る says it is possible, the opposite of the feeling here.
tell: Mind verb (信じる・受け入れる・理解する) + がたい = emotionally hard.

s: 今回のようなシステム障害は、どの銀行でも起こり（　　）ことだと専門家は指摘する。
en: Experts point out that a system failure like this one could happen at any bank.
why: 得る = possible as an event; どの銀行でも shows it could happen anywhere.
がたい means hard to do, which contradicts 'at any bank'.
かねる is a polite refusal and never follows 起こる.
ようがない means it has no way to happen, the opposite of the point.
tell: Possible as an event (あり得る・起こり得る) → ます stem + 得る.

s: 大変恐れ入りますが、当店では他店で購入された商品の修理はお受け（　　）。
en: We are very sorry, but we are unable to accept repairs on items bought at other shops.
why: いたしかねます is the polite business 'we cannot'.
かねません means 'might well happen', the near opposite of a refusal.
得る says something is possible, which turns the apology into a yes.
わけです draws a conclusion and doesn't refuse.
tell: Polite business refusal → お〜いたしかねます. かねない = might well.

s: このまま無理な残業を続けさせていては、若手社員が次々に辞めてしまい（　　）。
en: If we keep making them do this much overtime, our young staff could well quit one after another.
why: かねない: the current situation could lead to something bad.
かねる means 'cannot (politely)' and is about the speaker's own action.
がたい means hard to do and goes with mind verbs.
ようがない means there is no way, which contradicts the warning.
tell: このまま〜ては + a bad outcome that could happen → ます stem + かねない.

s: このマンションは築年数の（　　）、設備が新しく内装もきれいだ。
en: For a building of its age, this block of flats has new facilities and a clean interior.
why: 名の + わりに: given its age, the result is better than you'd expect.
にしては attaches straight to a noun (築年数にしては), never after の.
せいで blames a cause for a bad result, but new fittings and a clean interior are good.
あまり needs too much of a feeling or state, leading to an extreme reaction.
tell: 名の + わりに; 名 + にしては (no の). Both mean 'for a ~', so the の decides.

s: 多くの高山植物（　　）、急な気温の上昇は生き残れるかどうかにかかわる問題だ。
en: For many alpine plants, a sudden rise in temperature is a question of survival.
why: にとって + an evaluation: how something rates from X's standpoint.
にしてみれば guesses at a person's feelings, and plants have none.
として means 'in the role of', which doesn't fit.
にしては needs a specific value and a surprising result.
tell: From X's standpoint + an evaluation (大切だ・問題だ) → にとって.

s: 地元の人たちが十年近く署名活動を（　　）、ついに念願の駅が町にできた。
en: After local people had campaigned with petitions for nearly ten years, the town finally got the station it had long wanted.
why: た形 + 末に: after long effort, an outcome finally came; 十年近く and ついに confirm it.
あげく ends in a letdown or a weary give-up, but 念願の駅 is a happy result.
たきり means nothing happened after that, but something did.
ずじまい means you never got round to it, but they did campaign.
tell: Long effort + ついに／ようやく + a hoped-for result → 〜た末に. あげく ends badly.

s: 高校時代の友人に「また連絡するね」と言われた（　　）、もう五年も音沙汰がない。
en: An old school friend told me, 'I'll be in touch,' and I haven't heard a word in the five years since.
why: たきり: did X and nothing since; もう五年も音沙汰がない confirms it.
たところ reports a result found right after one action.
末に needs long effort before it.
あげく needs a long ordeal before it.
tell: Did X, and nothing since (〜ない after) → 〜たきり.

s: 後ろから声をかけてもらわなかったら、危うく反対方向の電車に（　　）。
en: If someone hadn't called out from behind me, I would very nearly have got on a train going the wrong way.
why: 危うく + dictionary form + ところだった: it nearly happened, but didn't.
た形 + ところだった means 'had just got on', which contradicts the near miss.
ずじまい means you meant to and never did, the wrong meaning.
たきり means nothing happened after, which doesn't fit.
tell: 危うく／うっかり + dictionary form + ところだった = nearly.

s: このチャンスだけは、たとえ有給休暇を全部（　　）、絶対に逃したくない。
en: This chance is one I don't want to miss, even if it means using up all my paid leave.
why: てでも: an extreme means plus the speaker's own resolve (逃したくない).
てまで criticises someone for going too far, not the speaker's resolve.
さえ means 'even' and cannot be followed by a wish.
くらい marks a trivial minimum, not an extreme means.
tell: Extreme means + my own wish or resolve → 〜てでも. てまで criticises.

s: 注目を集めたいからといって、立ち入り禁止の場所に（　　）写真を撮るのはどうかと思う。
en: Wanting attention is one thing, but I have my doubts about going into restricted areas just to take photos.
why: てまで: going as far as an extreme means, with criticism (どうかと思う).
くらい marks a trivial minimum, but trespassing is not trivial.
さえ means 'even' and needs a negative or a conditional after it.
など belittles something and cannot link straight to 写真を撮る.
tell: Going too far + criticism (どうかと思う・気が知れない) → 〜てまで.

s: いくら忙しくても、休むときは電話の一本（　　）入れるのが社会人としての常識だ。
en: However busy you are, it's basic courtesy for a working adult to at least phone in when taking time off.
why: くらい marks the bare minimum: at least one phone call.
まで marks something extreme, but a phone call is the minimum.
さえ (even) goes with a negative, as in 一本さえ入れない.
など belittles X, which clashes with calling it 常識.
tell: The bare minimum you should manage → 〜くらい(ぐらい).

s: 異動してきた当初は、社内の略語（　　）、会議の内容が半分も理解できなかった。
en: When I first transferred, I didn't even know the in-house abbreviations, so I couldn't follow half of what was said in meetings.
why: さえ + negative: not even something this basic.
さえ〜ば is a condition, and it doesn't fit a past fact.
まで marks an extreme, and knowing it would not leave you lost.
くらい marks an easy minimum, and knowing it would not leave you lost.
tell: Not even something basic (〜さえ〜ない) vs if only (〜さえ〜ば): check the ending.

s: この申請書（　　）、あとは窓口に出すだけなので、今日中に片付けてしまおう。
en: Once I finish this application form, all that's left is to hand it in, so let's get it done today.
c: くらい書き終えたのに
why: さえ〜ば: this one step is enough; あとは〜だけ follows.
さえ + negative means 'not even', which contradicts あとは〜だけ.
など belittles X, and ても gives the wrong logic.
のに shows regret over a past fact, which doesn't fit a plan.
tell: This one condition and the rest is easy (あとは〜だけ) → 〜さえ〜ば.

s: あの店はいつ前を通っても行列ができているところをみると、よほど味がいい（　　）。
en: Judging by the queue outside every time I pass, that shop's food must be really good.
why: ところをみると + とみえる: a guess from what you observe about others.
おそれがある is for the risk of something bad.
かねない attaches to the ます stem and is only for bad outcomes.
まい means 'surely not', the opposite of the guess.
tell: ところをみると + a guess about someone else → 〜とみえる.

s: 気象庁によりますと、この台風は明日の朝にかけて関東地方に上陸する（　　）。
en: According to the Meteorological Agency, there is a risk this typhoon will make landfall in the Kanto region by tomorrow morning.
why: おそれがある is the news word for the risk of something bad.
にきまっている is a spoken gut feeling, wrong for a weather report.
とみえる is a guess from one's own observation, not an agency forecast.
まい has no polite form, and it means 'surely not'.
tell: News or official warning of something bad → 〜おそれがあります.

s: 便利さばかりを追い求めてきた結果、私たちは待つ力を失ってしまった（　　）。数分の遅れにさえいらだつ人が増えている。
en: Having chased nothing but convenience, have we not lost the ability to wait? More and more people get irritated even at a few minutes' delay.
why: のではあるまいか puts forward the writer's view as a question (isn't it the case that…), and the next sentence backs it up.
のではあるまい without か means 'surely not', which denies the very point the next sentence supports.
とみえる is a guess about others from what you see, but 私たち includes the writer.
ものか is an angry spoken denial, the opposite of the writer's point.
tell: Essay thesis put as a question → 〜のではあるまいか. Without か, あるまい means 'surely not'.

s: 学生のころ、私たちは試験の前になるとよく誰かの部屋に集まって、朝まで（　　）。
en: When we were students, before exams we'd often gather in someone's room and talk until morning.
c: 語り合うものではない
why: た形 + ものだ: a fond memory of a past habit; 学生のころ and よく set it up.
Dictionary form + ものだ states a general truth, but 私たちは and 学生のころ make this a personal memory.
たいものだ is a wish, but this is about the past.
ものではない says what one shouldn't do.
tell: Our own past habit, remembered fondly (〜ころ・よく) → た形 + ものだ.

s: よその家に招かれたときは、出された料理を残さず（　　）と、子どものころ祖母によく言われた。
en: As a child, I was often told by my grandmother that when you're invited to someone's home, you should eat everything you're served.
why: Dictionary form + ものだ: how people should behave in general, a rule of manners.
ものか is an emotional refusal (I'll never eat it), not a rule of manners.
ことか needs a question word (どんなに・なんと) and exclaims; it cannot state a rule.
ものがある describes a quality you feel in something (胸を打つものがある), not a rule.
tell: General manners, how one should behave → dictionary form + ものだ (ものではない for 'shouldn't').

s: あれだけ毎日上司に怒鳴られて、よく平気な顔で（　　）。
en: Yelled at by the boss that much every day, it's amazing he can keep a straight face.
why: よく〜ものだ: being struck by something, here amazement.
たいものだ is a wish, which doesn't fit amazement at someone else.
ものではない gives a rule of behaviour, which clashes with よく.
ものか denies flatly, which clashes with よく (amazement).
tell: よく〜ものだ = amazement (how on earth can they ~).

s: 留学先で初めて母からの手紙を受け取ったとき、どんなに（　　）。
en: How happy I was when I got my first letter from my mother while studying abroad.
why: Question word (どんなに) + ことか: how very ~!
ことだ (exclamation) does not take a question word like どんなに.
ことはない means 'no need to'.
Verb + ことだ is advice, which doesn't fit.
tell: どんなに／なんと／何度 + 〜ことか = how very ~!

s: 締め切りは明日なのに、そのコンテストに申し込もうか（　　）、まだ決められずにいる。
en: The deadline is tomorrow, but I still can't decide whether to enter the contest or not.
why: Volitional + か + dictionary form + まいか: whether to do it or not.
ものか is an emotional refusal, and the speaker hasn't decided.
まいが pairs with ようが (no matter whether), not with ようか.
どころか means 'far from it', which breaks the pair.
tell: 〜ようか〜まいか = whether to or not (迷う・決められない).

s: 応募者のうち、実際に採用されたのは全体の3％（　　）。
en: Of all the applicants, only 3% were actually hired.
why: にすぎない downplays: merely, only this small amount.
にほかならない states 'nothing other than' and doesn't go with a small figure.
に越したことはない means 'best if', which doesn't fit a result.
というものだ gives a common-sense verdict on a situation, not a figure.
tell: A small amount or role, downplayed (全体の〜％・一社員) → にすぎない.

s: 海外で働くなら、現地の言葉が話せる（　　）。ただ、話せなくても仕事が回る職場も多い。
en: If you're going to work abroad, it's best to be able to speak the local language. Still, plenty of workplaces get by even if you can't.
why: に越したことはない: best if, though not essential; ただ、話せなくても〜 says it isn't required.
にすぎない downplays something as merely small.
にほかならない makes a flat claim of identity (X is nothing but Y), and it follows a noun.
というものだ gives a common-sense verdict on a situation, not a preference.
tell: Best if, but not essential (ただ／が、〜なくても) → 〜に越したことはない.

s: 高齢ドライバーの事故を減らすには、免許の返納を個人の判断に任せるのではなく、社会全体で支える仕組みを（　　）。
en: To cut accidents involving older drivers, society as a whole should build a system of support, rather than leaving licence return to individuals.
why: べきだ states the writer's view of what is right, as an editorial does.
にすぎない downplays something as merely small.
というものだ gives a verdict on an existing situation, not a proposal.
ものがある describes a felt quality, not a proposal.
tell: Writer's opinion of what should be done → dictionary form + べきだ (すべきだ).

s: 主力商品の売り上げがここまで落ち込んでは、価格の見直しも（　　）。
en: With sales of our main product down this far, we have no choice but to consider revising prices too.
c: 検討せずにはいられない
検討するわけにはいかない
why: ざるを得ない: circumstances leave no way out; する becomes せざる.
ずにはいられない is an urge you can't hold back, like laughing or crying, not a business decision.
わけにはいかない means 'we can't very well consider it', the opposite of the logic.
わけがない means 'there's no way we'd consider it', which ignores the slump.
cue: ここまで落ち込んでは
tell: Circumstances force it, reluctantly → ない形 + ざるを得ない.

s: 引っ越しの前日、親友とつまらないことで言い争ったまま別れてしまったことが、今でも（　　）。
en: Even now, I can't stop regretting that the day before I moved, I parted from my best friend after arguing over something trivial.
c: 悔やまずにはいられない
悔やんでしかたがない
why: ことが needs the spontaneous form 悔やまれる, and てならない marks a feeling welling up by itself.
悔やむ is an active verb, so 悔やまずにはいられない needs ことを, not ことが.
悔やんで also needs ことを; with が you need the spontaneous 悔やまれて.
にすぎない downplays something as minor, which clashes with lasting regret.
tell: 〜が + spontaneous verb (悔やまれる・思い出される) + てならない. With を, use the active verb.

s: 毎朝の満員電車のストレスを、どうにかして（　　）。
en: Isn't there some way I could cut down the stress of the packed train every morning?
why: どうにかして + ないものか: a hard wish phrased as a question.
ものなら needs a wish clause after it and cannot end the sentence.
た形 + ものだ is a fond memory of a past habit, not a wish.
ものではない gives a rule of behaviour, not a wish.
tell: どうにかして + 〜ないものか = isn't there some way? (a hard wish)

s: うちの新しい上司は、部下の名前（　　）まともに覚えていないのだから、私たちの仕事ぶりなど見ているはずがない。
en: Our new boss can't even get his staff's names right, so there's no way he's paying attention to how we work.
why: からして: even this basic thing (our names) is wrong, so the whole (how he sees our work) is suspect.
からすると gives a basis for judging something else, but the names are the very thing he gets wrong.
にとって gives someone's viewpoint plus an evaluation.
として means 'in the role of'.
cue: まともに覚えていない
tell: Even a basic detail is wrong, so the whole is suspect → 〜からして.

s: 結論（　　）、今回の企画は来年度に見送ることになりました。
en: To give you the conclusion first, this project has been put off until next year.
why: 結論からいうと is the neutral 'to start from the conclusion'.
からして picks a small detail as proof of a criticism.
に限って means 'of all times' and expresses bad luck.
にかけては praises a skill.
tell: A neutral basis for judging or speaking (結論から・立場から) → からいうと／からすると.

s: その職人は四十年間一日も（　　）、毎朝五時に工房の火を入れてきた。
en: For forty years that craftsman has lit the fire in his workshop at five every morning without missing a single day.
why: ことなく is the formal 'without': without missing a day.
のみ means 'only', which contradicts 一日も.
とのことだ reports what someone said.
において follows a noun and marks a place or field.
tell: Formal 'without ever' (一日も〜ことなく) → dictionary form + ことなく.

s: この坂は、昔、両側に椿の木がずらりと並んでいた（　　）、今でも「椿坂」と呼ばれている。
en: This slope is still called 'Camellia Hill' because camellia trees once lined both sides.
why: ことから gives the grounds for a name, and と呼ばれている follows.
ことに puts an emotion first (残念なことに), which doesn't fit.
ことは〜が repeats a word to concede a point.
こと alone is an instruction on a notice.
tell: Origin of a name (〜と呼ばれる・〜という名がついた) → 〜ことから.

s: 子どもが熱を出したと保育園から連絡がありましたので、本日は二時で（　　）。
en: The nursery has called to say my child has a fever, so may I leave early at two today?
c: 早退させていただけませんか
早退していただけませんか
早退なさってもいいですか
早退させてさしあげませんか
why: させていただけませんか humbly asks permission for the speaker's own action.
していただけませんか asks the listener to leave early, the wrong person.
なさる is 尊敬語 for the listener's action, never your own.
させてさしあげる offers to let someone else leave, which reverses who is leaving.
tell: Asking to do something yourself → 〜させていただけませんか／させていただけないでしょうか.

s: 道に迷っていたら、通りかかった高校生が駅まで（　　）、本当に助かった。
en: I was lost, and a passing high school student walked me to the station. It was a real help.
why: 高校生が did me a favour, so てくれる brings the favour toward me.
案内されて would make the student the one being guided.
てあげる sends the favour away from me, but I was the one helped.
てもらう needs me as the subject (高校生に案内してもらって), not 高校生が.
tell: Someone else (が) does me a favour → 〜てくれる. With てもらう the subject is me.

s: 五歳の娘の何気ない一言に、私は自分の言葉づかいを深く（　　）。
en: My five-year-old daughter's offhand remark made me take a hard look at the way I speak.
why: Causative passive: the remark moved me to reflect, with 私は as subject and 一言に as the cause.
反省させた would mean I made someone else reflect.
てもらった means someone did it for me as a favour, but nobody reflected on my behalf.
てあげた means I reflected as a favour to someone, which makes no sense.
tell: Something moved me to think or feel (〜に〜させられた) → causative passive.

s: 駅に（　　）、改札を出る前に一度電話をください。
en: When you get to the station, please give me a call before you go through the ticket gate.
why: たら accepts a request after it: once you arrive, call.
と cannot be followed by a request.
たとたん is for a surprise that already happened and cannot be followed by a request.
ても means 'even if', which makes no sense with this request.
tell: A request after the condition → たら. と and たとたん refuse a request.

s: このアプリを使えば誰でもすぐに上手な写真が撮れると宣伝されているが、実際は必ずしも（　　）。
en: It's advertised that anyone can take great photos straight away with this app, but in reality that isn't necessarily so.
c: そうなるに決まっている
why: 必ずしも locks in a partial negative: とは限らない.
に違いない is the ending that きっと locks in, and it clashes with 必ずしも.
に決まっている is certainty and clashes with 必ずしも.
はずだ is a confident expectation and clashes with 必ずしも.
tell: 必ずしも → 〜とは限らない／〜わけではない.

s: 当ホテルの朝食は六時半から九時までです。（　　）、日曜日は七時からの営業となりますのでご注意ください。
en: Breakfast at our hotel is served from 6:30 to 9:00. On Sundays, however, it starts at 7:00, so please take note.
why: ただし adds an exception to what was just stated.
つまり restates the same point in other words.
そのうえ adds more of the same kind, not an exception.
なぜなら gives a reason and needs 〜からだ at the end.
tell: An exception to the rule just stated (hours, fees, eligibility) → ただし.
